title: GCS, decorticate and decerebrate
stem: A 58-year-old man was found on the pavement after an assault. He is on a trolley in resus with a collar on; airway, breathing and circulation have been assessed and are stable. The examiner asks you to assess his conscious level and neurological status, report your findings, and say what you would do.
notes:
Checked against the Glasgow Coma Scale teaching (Teasdale et al., Lancet Neurol 2014; glasgowcomascale.org), NICE NG232 (Head injury, 2023) and ATLS 11th edition.

The 2014 approach: check for factors that interfere (intubation, sedation, dysphasia, injury), observe first, then stimulate: spoken, then physical. Physical stimuli: fingertip (nail-bed) pressure peripherally, trapezius pinch or supraorbital notch pressure centrally. Sternal rub is not recommended (bruising, poorly standardised). Report each component (E, V, M), not just the total; score as 'NT' if a component cannot be tested, for example V when intubated.

Motor: 6 obeys, 5 localises (hand crosses above the clavicle toward the stimulus), 4 normal flexion (withdrawal), 3 abnormal flexion (decorticate: slow, stereotyped, arm across the chest, wrist flexed), 2 extension (decerebrate: arm straightens and turns in), 1 none. Use the best response of either arm.

Decorticate posturing points to a lesion above the red nucleus (hemispheres, internal capsule, thalamus). Decerebrate posturing points to midbrain or upper pons compression, below the red nucleus: worse. A change from flexion to extension, a falling GCS or a new unequal pupil means herniation.

Your notes list decerebrate and decorticate under ATLS without detail; nothing conflicts.

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Before scoring: has he had sedation or drugs? Any reason a component can't be tested?

opts.t: Any sedatives, opioids or alcohol? Any intubation?
opts.mark: Checks for factors that affect the GCS
opts.r: Nurse Ma: No drugs given. Smells of alcohol but the paramedics say he was talking at first.

opts.t: What was his GCS on arrival?
opts.mark: Asks the previous GCS to judge the trend
opts.r: Nurse Ma: GCS 12 on arrival 20 minutes ago.

steps.label: Assess conscious level
steps.hint: Observe, then speak, then a standard pressure stimulus. Report each component.

Eyes.t: Speak to him loudly: 'Mr Tang, open your eyes'
Fingertip pressure on the nail bed for 10 seconds
Eyes.mark: Uses a standard peripheral pressure stimulus

Eyes.t: Rub his sternum hard with your knuckles
Eyes.r: Sternal rub bruises and is not a standardised stimulus. Use trapezius pinch or supraorbital pressure.

Verbal.t: Ask his name, where he is, the month
Verbal.mark: Assesses orientation and scores verbal as V2

Motor.t: Ask him to squeeze your fingers and let go

Motor.r: Both arms flex slowly across his chest, wrists and fingers curled; legs extend and feet point.
Motor.mark: Uses a central stimulus and sees abnormal flexion (M3)

Motor.r: Now both arms straighten and turn inward, wrists flexed, legs extended, neck arched.
Motor.mark: Repeats the assessment and finds extension (M2)

Pupils.t: Pupil size and reaction to light
Pupils.r: Right 6 mm, unreactive. Left 3 mm, brisk.
Pupils.mark: Checks pupils: right fixed and dilated

Other.r: Boggy swelling over the right temple.
Other.mark: Looks for the site of the head injury

steps.label: Report to the examiner
steps.hint: Report components and the total, the posture and what it means, and the pupils.

opts.t: GCS E2 V2 M3 = 7, down from 12
opts.mark: Reports by component with the total and the trend

opts.t: Abnormal flexion (decorticate), now extension (decerebrate): M2, GCS 6
opts.mark: Recognises the change from flexion to extension as deterioration

opts.t: Right fixed, dilated pupil: right-sided mass lesion with uncal herniation
opts.mark: Interprets the fixed pupil as ipsilateral herniation

opts.r: A slow flexion of the arm across the chest is abnormal flexion (M3), not localising (M5).

steps.label: What now
steps.hint: GCS 6 with a blown pupil: airway, CT, neurosurgery, hyperosmolar therapy.

opts.t: Call the anaesthetist and prepare to intubate (GCS 8 or less)
opts.mark: Secures the airway: GCS 8 or less

opts.t: Head up 30 degrees, avoid hypoxia and hypotension
Urgent CT head and C-spine; call neurosurgery

opts.r: A fixed pupil means a mass effect; lumbar puncture can cause coning.

opts.t: Observe and repeat GCS in an hour
opts.r: He is herniating. This is an emergency.

CT.r: A right-sided crescentic hyperdense collection along the whole hemisphere, crossing sutures, with midline shift to the left.
CT.mark: Interprets CT: right acute subdural haematoma with shift

qs.q: What is the GCS motor score for decorticate (abnormal flexion) posturing?
Decerebrate posturing suggests a lesion where?
wrong: The cervical spinal cord at C5
qs.why: Below the red nucleus; decorticate posturing points to a lesion above it.

qs.q: How do you tell localising (M5) from withdrawal (M4)?
qs.a: The hand moves above the clavicle to the stimulus
wrong: The arm pulls away with normal flexion
The patient also opens the eyes to pain
The legs move as well as the arms each time

qs.q: How do you record verbal response in an intubated patient?
qs.a: Record V as T (not testable); give E and M
wrong: Score V1 as no verbal response
Leave the GCS out until extubation

qs.q: Which pupil sign suggests uncal herniation?
wrong: Horner's syndrome on the side of the clot

rules.fail: You acted before checking for drugs or factors that affect the GCS.

badge.name: Coma Counter
badge.flavor: E, V and M, never just the total. Flexion to extension means he's coning.

cards.why: M6 obeys, M5 localises, M4 normal flexion, M3 abnormal flexion, M2 extension, M1 none.

cards.q: Recommended central pressure stimulus for the GCS?
options: Sternal rub with the knuckles for 30 seconds
Pinching the nipple or inner thigh
Pressing firmly on the closed eyeball
cards.why: Sternal rub bruises and is poorly standardised.

cards.q: Arms extended and internally rotated, wrists flexed, legs extended: this is…
cards.why: Extension posturing indicates brainstem compression below the red nucleus.

cards.q: A GCS of 8 or less after head injury means…
options: Repeat the GCS in 30 minutes first
cards.why: NICE: intubate for GCS 8 or less.

cards.q: A new fixed dilated pupil on one side after head injury is due to…
options: Third nerve compression by uncal herniation
Sympathetic chain injury in the neck
Direct optic nerve injury on that side
cards.why: The uncus herniates over the tentorium and compresses the oculomotor nerve.

cards.q: Acute subdural haematoma on CT looks like…
options: A crescent that crosses suture lines
A lens shape that stops at the sutures
cards.why: Subdural blood spreads under the dura across sutures; extradural blood is limited by them.
